episode.title: How A Brewery Flooded London In 1814!

synopsis: A massive brewing vat rupture unleashed a destructive wave of porter beer through the slums of nineteenth-century London.
narration: In 1814, a ruptured vat unleashed five hundred seventy tons of fermenting porter through the narrow streets of London. The fifteen-foot tidal wave destroyed brick tenements and claimed eight lives before draining away into the earth.

shots.prompt: Vertical framing. Low-angle eye-level shot inside a dark, multi-story industrial brewery as a gigantic twenty-two-foot wooden vat explodes with violently snapping iron hoops, unleashing a catastrophic dark foaming torrent of porter smashing through brick warehouse walls into daylight.

Vertical framing. Medium tracking shot through a cobblestone alleyway in St Giles as dark frothing liquid surges past shattered wooden doorframes and overturned handcarts, swirling around brick basements under a gloomy overcast nineteenth-century London sky.

music: Frantic industrial copper percussion, distorted tavern violin riffs, and pounding wooden stomp beats driving a hard, relentless groove without pause, building suffocating tension with fast metallic scrapes and slamming bass hits, snapping off instantly mid-beat to cycle seamlessly back to the start.
